Tracker.Contracts.select_exec:1307159cc4.description: The lemma states that, for any list xs, integer bounds s and e, and Boolean mode, calling selectPieces_val with their encoded values terminates and returns the encoded list obtained by filtering xs, preserving order. Tracker.Contracts.statev:ad87f46a7939a88.description: statev represents a tracker state as a StructV with two components: its shifts list encoded recursively by listv using nilv and nodev, and its pending value encoded as an integer literal, using -1 for None and p for Some p. Tracker.Contracts.structv_closed:a991748.description: The lemma states that if every value in the list vs satisfies closed_val, then the structure value StructV vs also satisfies closed_val. The input does not define closed_val, so the precise meaning of “closed” is not established.

Tracker.Model.add_pair:430282e938794e91d.description: add_pair checks a proposed pair of endpoints s and e in order: it returns code 1 if s is negative, 2 if e ≤ s, 4 if pending contains a value p with p < e, or 3 if the overlap test succeeds against existing shifts. Each failure preserves the original state and returns no rows. Otherwise, it returns code 0, preserves pending, and inserts split_daily s e before the first existing shift whose start is at least s, or at the end if none qualifies; it also returns no rows. The supplied input does not establish the exact splitting behavior, overlap criterion, or endpoint units.

Tracker.Model.add_query_round_trip:4b233.description: The theorem states that if every existing shift has a nonnegative start and ends strictly after it starts, and adding the interval from s to e succeeds with code 0, then querying the updated state over that same interval returns exactly the list split_daily s e, in either query mode. Successful addition implies 0 ≤ s < e, no reserved endpoint, and no overlap with existing shifts. The query selects shifts using hit in one mode and full containment in the other; the exact definitions of hit, reservation, and daily splitting are not supplied.

Tracker.Model.add_success:3a6af3632f9ff6.description: The lemma states that if add_pair st s e returns code 0, then s is nonnegative, s < e, the reservation and overlap checks are false, and the updated state contains split_daily s e inserted into the existing shifts using splice, with pending unchanged. The reservation condition means pending is absent or its value is at least e. Splice inserts before the first shift whose start is at least s, or appends if none exists. The precise overlap test and splitting behavior are not established because hit and split_fuel are not supplied.

Tracker.Model.answer:bd3ea779fca99fb4576.description: The record answer, constructed with Answer, contains an integer code, a tracker named updated, and a list of shifts named rows. Tracker.Model.boundary:05716a4353c0fd248.description: For integers s and e, boundary returns the smaller of e and s minus its remainder on division by 1440 plus 1440. The name next_midnight suggests a time cutoff, but the input does not establish time units or assumptions on s that justify interpreting it as the next midnight.

Tracker.Model.boundary_bounds:a45b1864d8.description: The lemma states that if s is nonnegative and e is strictly greater than s, then boundary s e is strictly greater than s and no greater than e. The boundary is defined as the integer minimum of next_midnight s and e; the supplied supporting lemma guarantees that next_midnight s is greater than s under the nonnegativity premise.

Tracker.Model.contained:6c0d8b8b37b9d50c.description: The definition contained takes integer bounds s and e and a shift x, which is a pair of integers, and returns true exactly when s is at most x’s first component (its start) and x’s second component (its finish) is at most e. It does not require the start to be at most the finish or s to be at most e.

Tracker.Model.daily_valid:f7b90e69583a81.description: A shift x is daily_valid when its start (the pair’s first component) is nonnegative, its finish (the second component) is strictly later, and it finishes no later than the next multiple of 1440 strictly after its start. The names suggest this boundary represents midnight, but the input does not specify the time units.

Tracker.Model.delete_shift:af0966f056f37.description: delete_shift takes a tracker state and a value s. If s is negative, it returns code 1 with the state unchanged. Otherwise, if any shift has start value s (its first component), it returns code 0 with all such shifts removed and pending unchanged; if none matches, it returns code 6 with the state unchanged. Every result contains an empty rows list. This is a function definition, not a correctness or termination claim.

Tracker.Model.deletion_preserves_invaria.description: The theorem states that, for any state st satisfying state_invariant and any s, the updated state returned by delete_shift st s also satisfies that invariant: its shifts are ordered and daily-valid, and any pending start is nonnegative and at least every shift’s finish. Successful deletion removes all shifts whose start equals s and preserves the pending value. Negative s or no matching shift leads to failure; the failure function’s behavior is not supplied. The exact meanings of ordered and daily_valid are also unspecified, and no proof is included.

Tracker.Model.duplicate_rejected:574dff9.description: The theorem states that if adding the interval from s to e to state st returns code 0, then adding that same interval to the resulting state returns a nonzero code. The initial success requires 0 ≤ s < e, a false reservation check at e, and no overlap with existing shifts; it inserts the interval’s daily pieces while preserving pending. Thus a successful addition makes an immediate duplicate unsuccessful, although the theorem does not specify the second error code.

Tracker.Model.empty_invariant:5e4e0e7b5c.description: The theorem states that a tracker with an empty list of shifts and no pending value satisfies the state invariant. This invariant requires the shifts to be ordered and every shift to satisfy daily_valid; the latter holds vacuously for an empty list, while the pending-value condition is automatically true for None. The input does not define the precise meanings of ordered or daily_valid.

Tracker.Model.end_preserves_invariant:8a.description: The theorem states that if a tracker’s state invariant holds before end_shift is called with an end value e, it also holds for the updated state in the returned answer, with no success-code premise. The invariant requires ordered shifts, every shift satisfying daily_valid, and, when a pending start exists, that start being nonnegative and at least every recorded shift’s finish. The claim covers both success and failure outcomes. The supplied input does not define ordered, daily_valid, or failure, so their precise meanings and behavior cannot be established here.

Tracker.Model.end_shift:06694526f60a3dcc.description: end_shift attempts to finish the pending shift at endpoint e. If no start is pending, it returns error 5 with the original state. Otherwise, it calls add_pair with the pending start and pending cleared: a negative start gives error 1, an end at or before the start gives error 2, a reserved end gives error 4, and an overlap gives error 3. Success returns code 0, shifts computed using split_daily and splice, and no pending start; failure returns the error code with the original state, preserving its pending start. All returned row lists are empty. The helper definitions are not supplied, so their precise behavior is unspecified here.

Tracker.Model.ends_after:7b36099993a6043.description: ends_after xs s returns a Boolean indicating whether any element x in xs has a finish value strictly greater than s; finish x is the second component of x. It returns false for an empty list. The supplied input does not specify the component types or the exact comparison represented by <?.

Tracker.Model.filter_all:ed741b22d7c6316.description: For a Boolean predicate f on shifts, where each shift is a pair of integers, this lemma states that if f returns true for every element of the list xs, then filtering xs with f leaves the list unchanged.

Tracker.Model.finish:c78e80afbd7dae28b94.description: finish takes a shift, which is defined as a pair of integers, and returns the second integer in that pair.

Tracker.Model.next_midnight:56e2b577d6e5.description: next_midnight takes an integer s, subtracts its signed remainder on division by 1440, and adds 1440. Tracker.Model.next_midnight_bounds:49acf.description: For any nonnegative integer s, the lemma states that next_midnight s, defined by subtracting the remainder of s divided by 1440 and then adding 1440, is strictly greater than s and at most s + 1440. This describes the next strictly later multiple of 1440, including when s is already a multiple; the input does not specify time units.

Tracker.Model.ordered:9aab792207cf3f4a74.description: The definition ordered describes lists of shifts, each represented by a pair of integers whose first component is its start and second is its finish. Tracker.Model.splice_contains:3b9e44ea21.description: The lemma states that any shift x occurring in ps also occurs in splice s ps xs. Here splice inserts ps into xs before the first shift whose start (its first component) is at least the integer s, or at the end if no such shift exists; no ordering assumption on either list is required.

Tracker.Model.splice_elements:7d95d8ea39.description: The lemma states that if x belongs to splice s ps xs, then x belongs to ps or xs: splicing introduces no new elements. Here splice inserts ps before the first element of xs whose start (its first component) is at least the integer s, or appends ps if no such element exists. The only premise is membership in the result; no assumption that either list is sorted is required.

Tracker.Model.splice_forall:d6df54bee540.description: The lemma states that if every shift (a pair of integers) in each of the lists ps and xs satisfies a property P, then every shift in splice s ps xs also satisfies P. The splice function inserts ps before the first element of xs whose first coordinate is at least s, or appends ps if there is no such element. No assumption that either list is sorted is required.

Tracker.Model.splice_ordered:ebcdfe5d739.description: The lemma states that inserting the list ps into xs before the first shift starting at or after s (or at the end if none does) preserves ordering: each shift finishes no later than any later shift starts. It assumes both lists are already ordered, every shift has a nonnegative start strictly before its finish, every shift in ps starts at or after s and finishes at or before e, and no shift in xs both starts before e and finishes after s.

Thus, with sufficient fuel, the returned intervals cover every point in [s, e).

A shift’s start and finish are its first and second components. The supplied definitions do not establish what makes the splitting “daily” or whether the covering shift is unique.

Tracker.Model.split_inside:b596f260c5478.description: The lemma states that if s is nonnegative, every shift produced by split_fuel fuel s e has a nonnegative start, finishes strictly after it starts, lies within the bounds s and e, and finishes no later than next_midnight of its start. The function terminates by decreasing its natural-number fuel, but limited fuel may leave part of the interval uncovered; this lemma does not assert complete coverage.

Tracker.Model.split_ordered:9844410d17ec.description: The lemma states that if s is nonnegative, then for any natural-number fuel and integer endpoint e, split_fuel fuel s e produces an ordered list of shifts: every earlier shift finishes no later than every later shift starts. The function stops when fuel runs out or e is at most the current start, so the lemma does not guarantee that the resulting shifts cover the entire interval up to e.

Tracker.Model.split_selected:782bfdb8515.description: The lemma states that if the integer bounds satisfy 0 ≤ s < e, every shift returned by split_daily s e lies within those bounds (s ≤ start and finish ≤ e) and satisfies the strict overlap checks (start < e and s < finish). The definition of split_fuel is not supplied, so the input does not establish exactly how these shifts are constructed or whether they cover the whole interval.

Tracker.Model.start:965262a461b40a749d7e.description: The definition start takes a shift, defined as a pair of integers, and returns its first integer component. The supplied input gives no further meaning to that component and states no additional premises.
